summary: Creates one active sample per off-to-on event and manages overlapping ADSR-style event lifetimes for MIDI, keyboard, Python, or other trigger sources.

key_params.name: input
key_params.note: Output input value captured at event birth

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: DAT with onCreate() and onDestroy() callbacks

key_concepts: Manages the birth and lifetime of overlapping off-to-on events, especially MIDI, keyboard, and Python-triggered events.
Generates one active sample per event until that event's attack, decay, sustain, and release lifetime completes.
Input 0 triggers events, input 1 resets events, and optional input 2 samples values for each event.
Output channels can include id, index, active, input, time, adsr, and state so downstream instancing can track event state.
The state channel moves through attack, sustain/loop, and release ranges and can drive phase-like controls such as movie offsets.
Callbacks DAT supports onCreate() and onDestroy() hooks for event lifecycle handling.
common_gotchas: Event CHOP creates samples for active events, not one fixed channel per note or trigger.
The first input triggers events, the second resets events, and the optional third input samples values for each event.
Many overlapping triggers can create many samples; downstream instancing should handle changing sample counts.
The id channel is useful for stable randomization or per-event lookup because event indices can shift as events die.
Callbacks should be validated because generated code can run on event creation and destruction.
